In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CETSCALE is a valid measure of consumer ethno-centrism in Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic.
the 10-item CETSCALE is not appropriate for use in the Czech Republic.
the CETSCALE should be considered a "good" measure for the Czech Republic, a "moderately good" measure for Hungary and a "good" but "not optimal" scale for Poland.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modified CETSCALE has been validated for use in Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic and that the scale can be applied in a cross national research setting.
the CETSCALE is a good instrument for the measurement of ethnocentrism in the Czech Republic and Hungary, but that it needs to be modified in Poland.

The main takeaway from our work is that
researchers should not assume the CETSCALE is a valid and reliable measure in all countries.
the 10 items CETSCALE should not be used in these central and European countries as a single scale, but rather as a multi-item scale with the number of items depending on the country.
